review_reference: Coordinator's tasks of 17 Nov 2026 on hid-system#258 (Q94 way of working): port main 0089 (hid-system#73, 'keep the chosen facility across reload') onto staging as 0129, booked there; the design note on #258 and the decisions on it (STAFF_FACILITY_SELECTION_MODE off | keep | ask, off by default; a failed read on GET /auth/session answers 200 with 'unavailable'; foreign keys to the sign-in, account, facility and membership, ON DELETE RESTRICT, as #262; the failure-audit fix is not part of this change). To be signed by the owner. Releases after 0128 (0124-0127 were released by #267 under Q98); production's pending set is then exactly 0129.
evidence: Migration 0129_session_facility_selection.sql (sha256 65705c33e1e55fd76bb06f8c19205391534c1b94b43ce890f17b82fec30ef360) and its runtime-grants.sql block (file sha256 f10887501247647276a823f4adfc0dfb55cddfbc30f8f622727c9e824893a098). WHAT IT DOES: a new table auth.session_facility_selection, one row per staff sign-in (session family, keyed by family_id, the id of the family's first session; refresh keeps the family), with account_id, facility_id, membership_id, selected_at and row_version: the facility a staff member chose with POST /auth/facility, so a reload, a new tab or a refresh opens there instead of silently at the primary facility. Four foreign keys, all ON DELETE RESTRICT: auth.sessions(id), auth.accounts(id), identity.facilities(id), and identity.staff_facility_memberships(id, facility_id, account_id) through 0002's unique key (so the membership is the account's at that facility, and the demo and QA seals of 0098 and 0123 hold through it). No row-level security (like auth.sessions). The guard auth.guard_session_facility_selection_change() (plpgsql, SECURITY INVOKER, search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp, every name qualified, revoked from PUBLIC, granted to no role) and its trigger session_facility_selection_guard (BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE, FOR EACH ROW) refuse a delete and a move to another sign-in or account (55000 SESSION_FACILITY_SELECTION_IMMUTABLE) and admit a row only for the first session of a staff sign-in of that account with a live session (not revoked, not expired) at the account's current token version, an active account not disabled, and an active, unheld membership of that account at that facility with an active verified staff record, active organisation and active facility (else 23514 SESSION_FACILITY_SELECTION_INVALID): the staff context's own conditions. Grants, in the migration when the role exists and identically in runtime-grants.sql: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE on the table to hid_identity_runtime (its API login inherits them); no DELETE or TRUNCATE; nothing to any other role or PUBLIC. No existing row, function, policy or grant changes. The row grants nothing: every facility-scoped request still carries X-Facility-ID, checked by the Identity guard, the access token has no facility claim, and identity-api re-checks the stored facility against the actor's current facilities for the session's own product on every read. NOT PORTED from main 0089: auth.lock_account_sessions (main 0073; the write locks the presented session FOR SHARE instead), the staff two-step sign-in (main 0088). DIFFERENCES from main: the guard also checks the account (active, not disabled) and the token version, uses search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp, and the grants are made in the migration. PRECONDITIONS (catalog reads, each a presence check; 55000 or 42501, nothing applied): 0001-0127 applied, the base it is proved on (0123's identity.sealed_qa_members, 0124's lab.work_item_patient_cards(uuid[]), 0125's pharmacy.work_item_prescription_details(uuid[]), 0126's identity.organization_staff_kinds(uuid) and 0127's auth.session_single_sign_on, read from pg_class and pg_proc, as 0125-0127 check the migrations before them; 0129 uses nothing 0124-0127 add, and 0128 is checked once #264 lands); not yet applied (no table, guard or trigger of those names, else '0129: already applied'); every column the guard and the keys read, by name and type; the primary keys (id) of auth.sessions, auth.accounts and identity.facilities and the memberships' unique (id, facility_id, account_id), by exact column set; the applier owns, or inherits from the owner of, those four tables and may create in schema auth (42501). No earlier function is replaced or called, so there are no md5 pins of earlier bodies. POST-CHECKS: columns, keys and their actions, no row-level security, the guard's body (md5 f77032f5b5082fed66f7b01a3ee34f5a), attributes, owner and ACL, the trigger, the exact table privileges (the owner, and SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE, not grantable, to hid_identity_runtime when that role exists; any other grantee stops the file with the ACL in its message, whether or not hid_identity_runtime exists, because the role is compared null-safely: on a fresh install, before the roles are made, a default privilege to another role is refused as it is on an upgrade), and the guard fired once with random ids answering exactly 23514 SESSION_FACILITY_SELECTION_INVALID (its first run plans every query in it, so every column it reads exists). LOCKS: SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on auth.sessions, auth.accounts, identity.facilities and identity.staff_facility_memberships (the four foreign keys), ACCESS SHARE on identity.staff and identity.organizations (section 5's firing of the guard reads them) and on every index of the six tables (creating the foreign keys takes the referenced keys' indexes; planning the guard's query takes the rest), and ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the new table, held to commit (47 relation locks, measured with pg_locks). Section 1 takes them first, in one attempt: the six tables NOWAIT, their indexes by planning a query on the six under a 10 ms lock_timeout. When 0129 is the first statement of its transaction (the runner applies each file in its own transaction), a busy table or index makes it try again every 100 ms for at most 5 s, else 55P03 '0129: ... stayed busy for 5 seconds; nothing applied', so it never waits while holding a lock and nothing queues behind it. When its transaction already holds an earlier migration's lock of mode SHARE or stronger on a table outside the runner's migration schema (the runner's dry run runs every pending file in one transaction: with 0128 pending, 0128's SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on identity.outbox_events), it makes one attempt and does not sleep: 55P03 '0129: ... is busy, and this transaction already holds an earlier migration's locks, so it does not wait; nothing applied; run the release again at a quieter time', within tens of milliseconds, instead of keeping those locks held for up to 5 s (Rahman, #258). The previous file took identity.staff, identity.organizations and the indexes after its loop: behind an ALTER TABLE, VACUUM FULL or REINDEX of identity.staff or identity.organizations, or an ALTER INDEX ... SET TABLESPACE of auth.sessions_pkey, it waited for the runner's 5 s lock_timeout holding the four tables (a sign-in write queued about 3.1 s), then stopped with section 5's 55000 (or, waiting for the index in section 2, with the lock timeout itself). Reads are never blocked (the ACCESS SHARE locks stop only DDL, VACUUM FULL and REINDEX of identity.staff and identity.organizations until commit); sign-ins, refreshes, sign-outs and account or workforce changes wait until 0129 commits (applied in 22 ms recorded on the upgrade below; the table is new, nothing is scanned). BACKWARD COMPATIBLE: nothing reads or writes the table until identity-api runs with STAFF_FACILITY_SELECTION_MODE keep or ask (infra HID_STAFF_FACILITY_SELECTION_MODE, off by default); today's image, and the new image with the setting off, answer exactly as before. Turn the setting on only after 0129 is applied: with it on and the table or any of its three grants missing, identity-api refuses to start (the ECS deploy rolls back). The foreign keys add a check to deletes of sign-ins, accounts, facilities and memberships and to a change of a membership's id, facility or account; nothing on staging does either. TESTS: services/ehr-api/test/database/session-facility-selection.integration.sql (rollback-only, fictional data, through hid_identity_api_runtime): structure, privileges, the API's write (session FOR SHARE, upsert by family) and replacement, every refusal (patient sign-in, later session, another account's sign-in or membership, membership of another facility, signed-out or lapsed sign-in, ended or held membership, inactive or unverified staff, suspended facility, deactivated organisation, locked or disabled account, older token version, no sign-in), two roles at one facility, refused moves and deletes (the owner's too), rotation, sign-out, a facility suspended and an account disabled through the platform commands and a membership ended or held with a row present (all succeed, the same choice is then refused), and the demo and QA seals; and the sign-in as its family's first session (Rahman's review on #258): a family whose first session is a patient session or another account's, or whose only live session is a patient session or another account's, is refused even with a live staff session of the account in it, an account-only outreach session (Q88-2: a staff session of a verified staff login with no active membership) is refused directly and through the API's write, and a sign-in rotated twice, whose first session is revoked and whose third is live, makes its first choice (an INSERT) keyed to the revoked first session; and single sign-on (0127): a staff sign-in a product issued after single sign-on (a root staff session with its auth.session_single_sign_on row) keeps a choice through the API's write and a refresh as a password sign-in does, a back-channel logout of its provider session (revocation_reason 'sso_logout', SsoService's own UPDATE as the Identity runtime) ends it exactly as sign-out does (no read, the API's write finds no live session, the row cannot be changed, 23514, and stays with the provenance row), a password sign-in outside that provider session keeps its choice until product sign-out ends every staff sign-in of the account, and the sign-in's first session cannot be deleted while either row refers to it (23503). identity-api's facility-selection-sso.spec.ts proves the same through the real single sign-on controller, service and session-end filter, with Q97 and 0126 narrowing a choice to 'reselect' for a single sign-on sign-in exactly as for a password one, and service-session byte for byte unchanged. PROVED 2026-11-17 and 2026-11-18 (re-proved on 2026-11-18 after staging 645252df, #267, was merged in: 0124-0127 released under Q98), and again on 2026-11-19 for the file at the sha256 above (section 1's one-attempt rule, and identity.staff, identity.organizations and the six tables' indexes taken in section 1; nothing else changed), with staging a9196203 (#278, no migration) merged in, on throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 clusters (fictional data only, deleted afterwards), schema owned and migrated by a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS login (MIGRATION_TARGET=rds), runtime grants applied by the cluster superuser as security administrator: UPGRADE from staging a9196203's 128 files (0001-0127, as 645252df's) by staging's own runner, with staging's runtime-grants.sql and runtime-roles suite; then this branch's runner: plan exactly [0129] at the sha256 above; dry run rolled back (no table, 128 recorded); applied (execution_ms 22); 0 pending; the file again by psql answers '0129: already applied'; the migration granted exactly SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE to hid_identity_runtime (and through it hid_identity_api_runtime) and nothing else (2492 runtime privileges before, 2498 after), and this branch's runtime-grants.sql then changed no runtime privilege; bootstrap, --verify-only and the new suite pass; the locks held to commit are the ones listed under LOCKS. npm --prefix services/ehr-api run db:test-staging-upgrade (HID_REHEARSAL_ADMIN_URL, with HID_BASELINE_RUNTIME_GRANTS set to staging a9196203's runtime-grants.sql, byte-identical to 645252df's, production's file today; the default baseline from git, the parent of the commit that added 0129, is 6364e4a1's file without 0124-0127's grants, so it no longer describes the base): passed (baseline 128, integrated 129, declared [0129], dry run rolled back, checksums preserved, migration grants equal runtime-grants.sql over 2651 privileges, 208 tables' row-level security unchanged, the no-FORCE baseline, clean install). FRESH install of all 129 files, by the superuser and by the NOBYPASSRLS login: plan, dry run, apply, 0 pending, bootstrap and --verify-only pass. Database suites (101: 17 in database/tests, 84 in test/database): all 101 pass when the schema owner is the cluster superuser (as scripts/run-container-database-acceptance.sh builds it); 99 pass under the NOBYPASSRLS owner, where schema.integration.sql (RLS on ocr.job_events) and records-processing-draft.integration.sql (case 6n) fail exactly as they fail on staging 645252df without 0129 (staging's migrations, runner and both suites are unchanged since). The new suite fails without 0129 (the table does not exist) and passes after it; with the guard's body check lifted it also fails for each of 21 weakened guards (run on an earlier file of this branch; the guard and the suite are unchanged since) (no token version, account status, disabled check, root session, revocation, expiry, hold, membership active, staff active, verification, organisation or facility active, membership account or facility, move or delete refusal, the first session's kind or account, the live session's kind or account, and a guard that wrongly requires the first session itself to be live). REFUSALS, each nothing applied (no table, guard or trigger; the ledger as before), run on the previous file (sections 0 and 2-5, which they exercise, are unchanged since): on 0001-0126, on 0001-0123, and on 0001-0127 with 0124's, 0125's or 0126's function dropped, 55000 '0129: 0001-0127 must be applied first'; a login that is not the owner, and a NOINHERIT member of the owner, 42501; memberships.migration_hold_reason dropped, 55000 naming it; auth.accounts.token_version made integer, 55000 naming it; the memberships' unique (id, facility_id, account_id) dropped, or replaced by unique (id, facility_id), 55000; a copy of 0129 whose guard reads a column that does not exist (its md5 pin adjusted) passes section 0 and is stopped by section 5's firing (42703 reported), nothing applied; on a base with no hid_ role (a fresh install before bootstrap-database-roles), the migrator's default privilege on new tables in schema auth granting another role SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE, DELETE, or SELECT WITH GRANT OPTION, 55000 '0129: the privileges on auth.session_facility_selection are not section 4's: ' and the ACL, and the same for SELECT with hid_identity_runtime present (a default privilege to PUBLIC is revoked by section 4, and 0129 then applies with only the owner, and hid_identity_runtime when it exists, in the ACL). LOCK PROOFS on this file (2026-11-19, the NOBYPASSRLS migrator, the runner's 5 s lock_timeout): an open write (ROW EXCLUSIVE) held 8 s on each of the four tables in turn: the runner stops after 5.10 to 5.12 s with 55P03 '... stayed busy for 5 seconds; nothing applied', and a third session's write on that table during the retries took 10 to 14 ms (no queue behind 0129); ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on identity.staff or identity.organizations, REINDEX TABLE of either, or ALTER INDEX auth.sessions_pkey SET TABLESPACE held 8 s: the same 55P03 from the loop after 5.1 to 5.7 s, while a write on auth.sessions took 11 to 17 ms (the previous file waited there and stopped after 5.16 to 5.26 s with section 5's 55000, or the lock timeout for the index, and that write took 3.1 to 3.2 s); with ACCESS EXCLUSIVE held on all 193 other application tables, 0129 applies (it takes no other table); a holder of 1.8 s on each of the four tables, or ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on identity.staff: the runner applies 0129 after 1.64 to 1.66 s (execution_ms 1540 to 1543). ONE ATTEMPT: in one transaction (lock_timeout 5 s) that already holds SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on identity.outbox_events (0128's lock), with any one of the four tables or identity.staff busy, 0129 stops 14 to 16 ms after it starts with 55P03 '... is busy, and this transaction already holds an earlier migration's locks, so it does not wait; nothing applied', nothing of 0129 applied, and a write on identity.outbox_events started during that transaction waited 519 to 522 ms, 500 of them the transaction's own pause before 0129 (the previous file: 0129 retried for 4978 ms and that write waited 5480 ms); with ACCESS EXCLUSIVE there instead, a reader of identity.outbox_events waited 522 ms (previous file 5492 ms); an earlier lock weaker than SHARE (ROW EXCLUSIVE) does not count: 0129 retries for 5 s. The runner: a dry run of [0129] alone behind a write on auth.sessions retries (the runner's ledger locks do not count) and stops after 5.09 s; a dry run of [0128 (#264's c2040ba3 file), 0129] on 0001-0127 behind that write stops in 144 ms with the one-attempt 55P03, nothing applied (the same dry run unblocked: 158 ms; with the previous 0129: 5110 ms); applying [0128, 0129] behind it commits 0128 in its own transaction, then 0129 retries and stops after 5.1 s (0128 recorded, 0129 not). Release checks: node scripts/verify-migration-ledger.mjs passes (129 migrations); npm --prefix release test (104 of 107) and npm --prefix release run verify fail only with 'components config.migration.files: missing migration prefix', because 0128 (#264) is not on this branch yet; with only that gap tolerated in a throwaway copy of the verifier, verify passes. REHEARSAL: scripts/tuf-staging-migration-rehearsal.mjs (a copy patched only for absolute paths, the cluster superuser and the cluster directory) passed in 4 min 13 s, 129 applied, every runtime check passing, facility_selection_runtime last. identity-api: 122 suites, 3335 tests pass (facility-selection-store.spec.ts reads this file); typecheck passes. RECOVERY: 0129 is one file in one transaction (the runner's dry run of the pending set, then the file), so any stop (55P03 when the six tables or an index of one stay busy, or at once when the dry run already holds an earlier file's locks; a precondition; a post-check) leaves nothing applied: production stays at its previous set, the plan is still exactly [0129], and the same release, with this declaration, can run again at a quieter time. This declaration lists only 0129, so a release whose pending set is anything else (for example 0128 not yet released) is refused before anything runs (UNREVIEWED_PENDING_MIGRATIONS); release 0128 first. ROLLBACK: an image rollback (production-backend-rollback changes images only) leaves the table, which older images ignore; to stop the behaviour, set HID_STAFF_FACILITY_SELECTION_MODE to off (stored rows are then ignored). A forward migration can drop the trigger, the guard and the table (the rows hold only sign-in, account, facility and membership ids and a time; no clinical data).
